title: Evaluation of the restricted chart cone map
statement: Let f:X→S be any scheme morphism, D:I→Over(S) a diagram of schemes, c a cone over D, i∈I and j an object of Over(i). Put B=D(i), P=X×_S B, Q_j=D(j.left)×_B P and Q_∞=c.pt×_B P. Let l:Q_∞→Q_j be the underlying canonical chart cone leg and assume its displayed second-projection equality l≫pr_P=pr_P. For an abelian étale sheaf F on X and q≥0, let G_j and G_∞ be its pullbacks along Q_j→P→X and Q_∞→P→X. Choose V étale over B, U étale over c.pt, and a specified pullback square U→V over c.pt→B. Let x be a restricted degree-q cohomology class on V×_B Q_j with coefficients G_j. Let z be the uniquely specified inverse image of x under the canonical raw cohomology comparison, and let z' be its raw pullback along l with the inverse upperStarComp coefficient identification. Then the apex chart cohomology comparison applied to the restricted-over cohomology cone map of x equals the specified single-free-representable pullback map for U→V followed by the apex raw-adjunction comparison applied to z'. No exchange map or stage lift occurs in this identity.

source.place: Second proof, evaluation side of the canonical comparison square; Tag 03Q8 for the raw cohomology comparison.

proof.text: Apply the existing chartRestrictedMap_eq_rawAffine to the chart cone leg and its displayed second-projection equality. That theorem is proved by reflexivity: restrictedOverCohomologyMap and rawAffineRestrictedCohomologyMap have the same literal derived-pullback and coefficient formulas; their commutativity proof arguments agree by proof irrelevance.
Apply rawRestrictedCohomologyClass_map to the canonical inverse-evaluation class of x. It identifies the raw affine map with evaluation of its raw pullback z'.

Use the proved defining equation cartesianChartRestrictedRawClass_eq to replace the raw pullback by the cached apex class. Apply the existing chartCohomologyIso_eval to that class, and compose with the preceding evaluation identity by congruence and transitivity. Neither exchange nor the stage lift occurs in this calculation.
